newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken mulls bank/life insurer links-paper.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken mulls bank/life insurer links-paper.

text.p: Swedish state-controlled bank Nordbanken sees good potential in mergers between banks and life insurers, Swedish business daily Finanstidningen reported on Monday.
"A merger between a bank and a life insurer is an interesting idea," Nordbanken chief executive Hans Dalborg was quoted as telling an analysts' meeting.
Dalborg referred to previous cooperation where banks created their own life insurers and insurers set up banking operations.
"There are evident merger gains on the life insurance side while there aren't any obvious links between non-life insurance and banking operations," Dalborg said.
He refrained from commenting on whether a merger with a life insurer would be profitable for Nordbanken.

Nordbanken's life insurance operations Livia only has 0.2 percent of new one-time premiums and 1.1 percent of annual premiums, while other bank-owned life insurers together have 60 percent and 24 percent respectively, statistics from the insurance association shows.
Dalborg said speculation about restructuring of the Swedish bank sector would continue for many years.
He said Nordbanken had no intention of increasing its number of branch offices but said it could belong to a larger group in the future.

The Swedish banking sector has already seen some change with banks joining forces ahead of expected competition when Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) starts in 1999 and ahead of the turn of the century, which will mean large computer costs.
Early this year Handelsbanken bought mortgage lender Stadshypotek for 22.9 billion crowns and Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced it intended to merge to become ForeningsSparbanken.
